beats.say: This is the Autopilot O.I. sales line. Twelve steps that turn a detailing shop's website into a paying customer, and nothing leaves the line without your yes.
It starts in the research lab. Agents read detailing shops' own websites, never LinkedIn, and save one real fact with the link where they found it.
The evidence gate checks every fact and scores the shop out of one hundred. No source, no lead. Phone only shops are held for a warm intro.
The draft writer opens with that real fact, adds the demo link, and offers two ways in: the thirty nine dollar kit, or the two ninety nine setup.
The claim check blocks anything untrue. No promise that it sends by itself, no guarantees, only real prices, and an opt out line in every email.
Then it stops at your desk. Five drafts are waiting right now. No yes, no send.
You send each one yourself, one to one, from your own email. The system has no send button at all.
The reply desk logs every answer and lists one follow up after four days. No thanks means never again.
When a shop is curious, the demo room shows the live demo and answers their questions.
They pay on Gumroad, and a private lead code rides along with the order.
The ledger only counts real payments. A reply is not a sale, and test orders and refunds are left out.
The safety vault keeps opt outs forever, keeps every shop's name private, and never spends without asking you.
Last, the pipeline report counts every step, and on day fourteen tells you to grow it, hold it or fix the offer. The lesson goes back to research.
One line, honest from start to finish. Your move: add your business address and approve the first five drafts.
